historical_references.context: Waliid ibn Al-Mundhir was a notable Banu Tamim tribal leader during the early Islamic period. He was the father of Zayd ibn Waliid, who was the first Arab to accept Islam and was the first to embrace the prophethood of Muhammad.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's 'Ansab Al-Ashraf' - Volume 4, page 345 The name Waliid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Waliid ibn Abd Al-Malik was the Umayyad Caliph Al-Walid I's third son. He was an influential figure in the Umayyad court and was the father of Hisham I, who ruled as the Umayyad Caliph from 724 to 743 AD.
